title: A Museum Tour Without a Script
title_ja: 台本のない美術館ツアー

source_links.title: Original fictional lesson — project authoring provenance, not factual evidence

fact_notes: 完全オリジナルの架空事例。実在の学校・人物・調査結果を示さない。リンクは制作方針の来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A small art museum asked students to be guides for a special afternoon event.
sentences.ja: 小さな美術館が特別な午後の催しの案内役を生徒たちに頼みました。

sentences.en: Mai prepared a long speech about a painting of a street on a rainy day.
sentences.ja: マイは雨の日の通りを描いた絵について長い説明を準備しました。

sentences.en: She practiced it many times because she wanted to remember every detail.
sentences.ja: 細部まですべて覚えたかったので何度も練習しました。

sentences.en: However, the first visitor asked a question that was not in her notes.
sentences.ja: しかし最初の来館者はメモにない質問をしました。

sentences.en: He wondered why the artist had painted a bright yellow window in the dark street.
sentences.ja: 画家が暗い通りに明るい黄色の窓を描いた理由が気になったのです。

sentences.en: Mai did not know the answer, so she invited him to look at the painting together.
sentences.ja: マイは答えを知らなかったので一緒に絵を見るよう誘いました。

sentences.en: Instead of guessing what the artist had intended, they described the colors and shapes they could see.
sentences.ja: 画家の意図を推測して断言する代わりに、目に見える色と形を描写しました。

sentences.en: Another visitor said that the window made her feel less lonely.
sentences.ja: 別の来館者は、その窓を見ると寂しさが和らぐと言いました。

sentences.en: Mai explained that this was a personal response, not a known fact about the artist.
sentences.ja: マイはそれが個人的な反応であり、画家について知られている事実ではないと説明しました。

sentences.en: By the end of the afternoon, Mai had learned to use her notes in a different way.
sentences.ja: 午後の終わりまでに、マイはメモを違う方法で使うようになりました。

sentences.en: She still shared the information she had prepared, but she also made time for visitors to speak.
sentences.ja: 準備した情報は伝えつつ、来館者が話す時間も作りました。

sentences.en: For her, a good tour became a chance to look closely at art with other people.
sentences.ja: 彼女にとってよいツアーとは、他の人と芸術をじっくり見る機会になりました。

vocabulary.definition: a place that displays objects or art

questions.prompt: What were the students asked to do?
What scene was in the painting?
options: A street on a rainy day

questions.prompt: Why did Mai practice her speech repeatedly?
options: She wanted to become the artist
She wanted to remember every detail

questions.prompt: What surprised Mai during the tour?
options: A question missing from her notes
A request to buy the painting
A sudden change in the painting

questions.prompt: What did the visitor ask about?
How did Mai respond when she did not know the answer?
options: She made up the artist's biography
She invited the visitor to examine the picture together
She told the visitor not to ask questions

questions.prompt: Why did they describe what they could see?
options: They knew the artist had left no paintings
It was a way to discuss the art without inventing the artist's intention
They wanted to change the painting
questions.explanation_ja: 見えるものに基づき、意図を断定しない。

questions.prompt: How did another visitor feel about the window?
Why distinguish a personal response from a known fact?
options: The guide knew every detail of the artist's life
A visitor's feeling does not establish what the artist intended
questions.explanation_ja: 感想と画家の事実は別。

questions.prompt: What did Mai learn about leading a tour?
options: The best tour is always a memorized speech
Prepared information and open discussion can work together
Visitors must agree about every artwork
questions.explanation_ja: 準備と対話を組み合わせた。

grammar.focus: that was not in her notes

grammar.explanation_ja: what節で画家の意図を表す。
関係代名詞の省略、過去完了。

paraphrases.source: She practiced it many times because she wanted to remember every detail.
paraphrases.rewrite: She rehearsed the speech to learn all the details.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 詳細を覚えるため練習した。

paraphrases.source: Mai did not know the answer, so she invited him to look at the painting together.
paraphrases.rewrite: Since she did not have an answer, she suggested looking at the picture together.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 答えが不明なので一緒に見ることを提案。

paraphrases.source: Mai explained that this was a personal response, not a known fact about the artist.
paraphrases.rewrite: Mai said the feeling belonged to the visitor and was not established information about the artist.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 観客の個人的反応と事実を区別。

paraphrases.source: For her, a good tour became a chance to look closely at art with other people.
paraphrases.rewrite: She came to see a tour as an opportunity for shared observation.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 共同で観察する機会だと考えた。

discourse.role_ja: 用意した説明と予想外の質問。
準備した説明に対話を加える対照。
